issue: Fill-color meaning shifts between the two cross-referenced figures on consecutive pages. In Fig 1.1, green marks the 'read for attention' stage and blue marks the input token boxes, while orange marks the append operation. In Fig 1.2, green marks Tokenizer and Embedding, blue marks Attention, and orange marks Token IDs. A reader who learns a color code from Fig 1.1 (the KV-cache detail) and carries it to Fig 1.2 (explicitly cited as 'the full token-travel pipeline') gets conflicting signals: green = attention-read vs. green = tokenize/embed; orange = KV append vs. orange = integer IDs. Purple is the only consistent mapping (stored K/V state in 1.1, KV Cache in 1.2). Each box is titled, so no meaning is lost, but the inconsistency invites false inference from color and undercuts the visual language the book will rely on in later chapters.
evidence: Fig 1.1 (PDF 27): 'read for attention' box filled green; token1..tokenn boxes filled light blue; 'append K/V' box filled light orange; stored K/V boxes filled light purple. Fig 1.2 (PDF 28): 'Tokenizer' and 'Embedding' boxes filled green; 'Attention' box filled light blue; 'Token IDs' box filled light orange; 'KV Cache' box filled light purple. The two figures are adjacent and cross-referenced in both captions ('the full token-travel pipeline is in Fig 1.2').
acceptance_test: Place Fig 1.1 and Fig 1.2 side by side and verify that each fill color denotes the same conceptual category in both (or that color is explicitly declared decorative in one shared caption note). Preferred fix: reserve purple = persistent KV state, blue = compute/attention, orange = token-level data, green = read/access, and recolor the mismatching boxes; then re-render both pages and confirm no box color contradicts its counterpart.
